events.reason: Sudden shortness of breath and left chest pain after coughing

reports.text: Portable AP view. Large left pneumothorax with collapse of the left lung and shift of the mediastinum to the right. Right lung shows chronic basal reticulation. No right pneumothorax.
reports.conclusion: Large left pneumothorax with mediastinal shift, consistent with tension physiology.

reports.text: Portable AP view after needle decompression and left chest tube placement. Left lung largely re-expanded with a small residual apical pneumothorax. Mediastinum midline. Chest tube tip at the left apex.
reports.conclusion: Left lung re-expanded after chest tube. Small residual apical pneumothorax.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside regional hospital ED, 02/02/2026.
CC: sudden breathlessness and left chest pain after a coughing fit.
HPI: 73-year-old man with COPD with chronic respiratory failure and IPF, on 2 L home oxygen and nebulizer, ICU stay last February for acute-on-chronic respiratory failure. This afternoon after a bout of coughing he felt a sudden sharp pain on the left side of his chest and could not catch his breath. Brought by his wife.
NKDA. Home meds per list.
Vitals: BP 145/90, HR 122, RR 28, SpO2 86% on room air.
Exam: anxious, tachypneic, tachycardic. Breath sounds diminished over the left chest without wheeze; hyperresonant to percussion on the left. Remainder of the exam unremarkable.
Portable CXR obtained at once: large left pneumothorax with rightward mediastinal shift.
Course: tension pneumothorax - needle decompression left second intercostal space, midclavicular line, with a rush of air and prompt improvement in heart rate and saturation; left chest tube then placed in the fifth intercostal space, anterior axillary line, under local anesthesia. Repeat film: lung re-expanded, small apical residual. SpO2 93% on 4 L.
Disposition: ICU for monitoring.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Outside regional hospital. Admitted 02/02/2026, discharged 02/06/2026.
Diagnosis: left tension pneumothorax, secondary spontaneous, in a patient with COPD and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
Course: Needle decompression and left chest tube in the ED. Two days in the ICU, weaned back to 2 L. Small air leak resolved by day 3; tube placed to water seal then removed on hospital day 4 with no recurrence on follow-up film. Pain controlled. Thoracic surgery reviewed; no pleurodesis at this time.
Discharge medications: unchanged home regimen - oxygen 2 L continuous, tiotropium, salmeterol, albuterol nebs as needed, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, metformin 1000 twice daily.
Advice: no air travel until cleared by pulmonology; return for any sudden breathlessness or chest pain.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within one week; pulmonology in 6 to 8 weeks with chest x-ray.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM. Tension pneumothorax on the left 2/2 after a coughing spell - needle decompression and chest tube in the ED, ICU 2 nights, tube out day 4, home 2/6. Records reviewed.
Now: chest tube site sore, improving. Breathing back to his usual on 2 L. No new sudden pain. Shaken by it. Wife did not leave his side.
Exam: sat as charted on 2 L. Left chest tube site clean and dry, sutured, no drainage. Breath sounds present both sides, basal crackles as before. Heart regular.
A/P: Left tension pneumothorax - resolved, clinically re-expanded. Suture out with nurse next week. Pulm f/u with CXR in April. Reviewed: call 911 for sudden chest pain or breathlessness. RTC May.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Suture Removal
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Single suture removed from L chest tube site. Healing well, no redness or drainage. Dry dressing. Pt says breathing feels like before the hospital.

documents.title: Portable tanks
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The oxygen company says my paperwork for the portable tanks runs out this month and they need you to sign again. Ingrid says hello.

documents.title: RE: Portable tanks
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Fred, we received their form this morning; it is signed and faxed back. Hello to Ingrid.

reports.text: PA and lateral. No pneumothorax. Bilateral basal reticular opacities, chronic. Lungs hyperinflated. No effusion. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: No pneumothorax. Chronic basal fibrotic change.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Pulmonology 4/14/2026. Left tension pneumothorax in February treated with decompression and chest tube; no recurrence. Back to baseline on 2 L. CXR today: no pneumothorax.
We discussed that recurrence risk is meaningful with his lung disease; he would prefer not to have pleurodesis unless it recurs, which is reasonable. Avoid air travel. Continue current inhalers and oxygen. Return in 6 months. NKDA.
Pulmonology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u. Pulm April: no recurrence, no pleurodesis for now. Feeling ok. Coughs carefully now, he says. No diarrhea, no jaundice. Swallowing same.
Exam: vitals as charted on 2 L. Lungs basal crackles, no wheeze. L chest scar healed. Abdomen soft. No edema.
A/P: COPD/IPF - baseline. Cirrhosis/HCC and pancreas - oncology surveillance next week. HTN, DM - labs today. RTC August.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Multiphase study. Treated pancreatic head mass, not changed in size. Biliary stent in place, no ductal dilation. Liver: ablation zone stable; no new lesion. No ascites. No adenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Stable. No HCC recurrence. No metastatic disease.

documents.title: Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Medical oncology 05/19/2026. Pneumothorax in February noted. CT 5/12 stable; CA 19-9 73, within the range of the past two years; AFP 5.1. Continue surveillance every 6 months. NKDA.
Medical Oncology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Summer f/u. Stayed out of the hospital since February. Oncology in May stable. Breathing at his usual on 2 L, nebulizer most mornings. Regurgitation now and then at night, unchanged. No diarrhea. Appetite fair, weight stable.
Meds reviewed - unchanged: O2 2 L, tiotropium, salmeterol, albuterol nebs PRN, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, metformin 1000 bid.
Exam: vitals as charted on 2 L. Lungs basal crackles. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, nontender. Feet intact to monofilament. No edema.
A/P: COPD with chronic resp failure / IPF - baseline. HTN - at goal. DM - A1c, BMP, urine microalbumin today. Cirrhosis/HCC s/p ablation and pancreatic cancer s/p SBRT - per hepatology/oncology surveillance. AWV and flu/COVID in the fall; front desk to call with a date.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Fred, yesterday's labs: kidney function and potassium normal, sugar control still good, blood counts similar to the spring, urine protein test normal. No changes needed.

documents.title: Hepatology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: hepatology
documents.body:
Hepatology visit 08/11/2026. Mr. Lindqvist remains abstinent, compensated, without ascites or encephalopathy. HCC surveillance is being done with his oncology multiphase CTs, most recently in May, without recurrence. Continue current care. NKDA.
Hepatology

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Can you send the metformin and the HCTZ to the pharmacy, 90 days please. Thanks.

documents.title: RE: Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Done - both sent for 90 days with refills.
